clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Meningitis.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

relationship_to_other_graphs.boundary_note: This graph targets meningitis recognition and verification; encephalitis graph should be loaded when encephalopathy, seizures, focal neurologic abnormalities, or brain inflammation features dominate.

basic_info.working_definition: Meningitis is inflammation of the meninges, commonly infectious; bacterial meningitis and meningococcal disease are time-critical emergencies.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Classic triad of fever, neck stiffness, and altered mental status may be incomplete.
Early symptoms can resemble viral illness, migraine, sepsis, influenza-like illness, or intracranial hemorrhage.
Rash may be absent in meningococcal disease.
Delays in empiric therapy, blood cultures, lumbar puncture decision-making, or sepsis recognition increase risk.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: When bacterial meningitis or meningococcal disease is suspected, urgent clinician-led empiric therapy and diagnostic pathway should not be delayed by incomplete workup.
do_not_use_as: a CSF interpretation tool without clinician review
a replacement for local meningitis/sepsis pathway

case_input_normalization.single_pass_missing_information_policy: Do not ask follow-up questions. Mark missing critical information explicitly and state how missingness affects verification.
case_input_normalization.normalization_patch_note: Normalization rules were systematized on 2026-06-28 to support retrieval from textual triggers, abbreviations, and numeric clinical facts. Rules map common case expressions to graph node ids where available. They are retrieval signals, not autonomous diagnostic criteria.

graph_nodes.name: Limb pain or cold hands and feet in meningococcal disease
Papilledema or signs of raised intracranial pressure
Positive Kernig or Brudzinski sign if assessed
Complement deficiency or complement inhibitor therapy
Blood cultures before antibiotics if this does not delay treatment
CSF glucose with paired blood glucose
CSF PCR or molecular testing when available
CT head before LP when indicated by red flags
Full blood count and inflammatory markers
Lactate and sepsis labs when severe illness
Low CSF glucose relative to blood glucose
Positive CSF Gram stain or culture
Do not delay empiric antibiotics for LP or CT when high suspicion
Assess need for adjunctive corticosteroid according to local protocol
Infection prevention and public health notification when meningococcal disease suspected
Critical care escalation for shock or reduced consciousness

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Fever/headache/neck stiffness/photophobia/altered mental status/seizure/rash or sepsis with possible CNS source.

strong_activation_patterns.reason: CNS infection possible; encephalitis also considered.
High-risk context with possible atypical presentation.

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are symptoms or signs suggestive of bacterial meningitis or meningococcal disease?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Treat as high-risk candidate and proceed urgently.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Lower priority but do not exclude early/atypical meningitis.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are sepsis, shock, reduced consciousness, seizure, focal deficit, or raised ICP signs present?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Escalate urgency and clinician-led emergency pathway.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Can blood cultures be obtained without delaying urgent empiric therapy?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Obtain cultures when feasible and do not delay treatment in high-risk cases.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is immediate lumbar puncture safe or is CT/stabilization needed first?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Proceed with LP if safe; otherwise CT/stabilize without delaying therapy.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: LP may be deferred if contraindications exist.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Do CSF results support bacterial meningitis?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Supports meningitis subtype and targeted management.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Negative early/partial data do not fully exclude if pretreated or high suspicion.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: CSF unavailable; diagnosis relies on clinical and blood/molecular evidence.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are encephalitis features prominent: encephalopathy, seizures, focal deficits, abnormal MRI/EEG?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Load encephalitis graph and consider parallel pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Meningitis remains primary if meningeal/sepsis features dominate.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is meningococcal disease suspected requiring infection control/public health actions?

distinguishing_features: Altered mental status lasting >24h, seizures, focal deficits, MRI/EEG abnormalities; overlap is common.
Thunderclap headache, vomiting, neck stiffness, focal deficit; CT needed.
Sepsis physiology with no meningeal signs or CNS findings; source may be urinary, lung, abdominal, skin.
Headache/photophobia/nausea; lacks fever, meningism, sepsis, altered mental status.
Often less severe, CSF lymphocytic pattern; bacterial disease must be excluded first in high-risk presentations.
Focal deficit, seizure, fever; imaging lesion.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: NICE NG240: Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management
evidence_sources.publisher: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
key_points: Covers recognition, diagnosis, and management of bacterial meningitis and meningococcal disease in babies, children, young people, and adults.
Used here for adult recognition, emergency treatment timing, lumbar puncture considerations, and meningococcal disease red flags.

evidence_sources.title: IDSA Clinical Practice Guidelines: The Management of Encephalitis
key_points: Provides diagnostic and treatment guidance for suspected encephalitis and multiple infectious etiologies.
Used here for encephalopathy-plus-inflammation recognition, CSF testing, neuroimaging, EEG, PCR testing, and empiric acyclovir consideration.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not wait for rash to suspect meningococcal disease.
Do not delay empiric treatment in high-risk suspected bacterial meningitis solely for CT or LP.
Do not exclude meningitis because the classic triad is incomplete.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always assess sepsis/shock and altered mental status.
Always consider encephalitis in AMS/seizure presentations.
